questions.q: Why do neighboring quadcopter propellers spin in opposite directions?
options: The firmware requires it for the mixer
questions.explain: Each motor tries to turn the frame in the direction opposite to the prop's rotation. Two pairs with opposite rotation compensate this torque.

questions.q: How does a quadcopter turn in yaw?
options: It tilts all the motors with servos
questions.explain: The difference in the reaction torques of the diagonal pairs creates a moment about the vertical axis with almost unchanged total thrust.

questions.q: What is a thrust-to-weight ratio (T/W) of 2:1?
options: Hover throttle of 20 % on a full battery
questions.explain: T/W = maximum thrust of all motors / takeoff weight. At 2:1 hover takes half the thrust — that is about 65–71 % throttle, because thrust grows faster than throttle; there is almost no margin for maneuvering.

questions.q: The drone flips over immediately on takeoff. The most likely cause?
options: High P and too powerful a battery
questions.explain: If the real build does not match the frame diagram in the firmware, the mixer commands the wrong motors, and the drone tumbles in a fraction of a second.

questions.q: Which control axis of a multirotor is the weakest, and why?
options: Pitch: the center of gravity is shifted
Yaw: the reaction torque is small
questions.explain: Yaw is produced by the reaction torque, which is much smaller than the moment from a thrust difference. So yaw is slower and is the first to hit motor saturation.
